transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is our weekly security sync for the Riverbank POC. We should have about 45 minutes.
[00:06] Lisa (CISO): Thanks, Maya. Busy week but we wanted to review a couple items: SSO, audit logs, and the retention windows while the pilot is on.
[00:12] Omar (Redwood SE): Morning all. I'll cover the logs and BYOK pieces, happy to dig into the VPC bits if needed.
[00:18] Mark (Platform): Quick note, Anita from compliance will push the retention questions.
[00:22] Anita (Compliance): Yep, thanks Mark.
[00:24] Maya: Great. First, SSO — last week we said we'd validate Okta SAML metadata. Mark, did you get a chance to pull that?
[00:30] Mark: I have the admin metadata, yes. We'll share, but want to confirm scope: are you doing SCIM for user provisioning or just SSO during the pilot?
[00:38] Omar: We support both. By default for the pilot we recommend SAML for auth and optional SCIM for provisioning so you can auto-provision RBAC groups. There was a small mismatch last week where SCIM role mapping didn't line up with your internal groups.
[00:50] Maya: Right, the mapping we showed in the demo was a suggested default, not prescriptive. For Riverbank we can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and enforce RBAC.
[00:58] Lisa: Important for us — we need SSO + MFA enforced through our IdP, and we want SCIM disabled until we validate least privilege. So SSO only for now.
[01:06] Omar: No problem. We support force-mfa via the IdP; we pass assertion and don't manage MFA ourselves. We will disable SCIM provisioning for the pilot environment.
[01:14] Anita: Also, how are admin actions logged? We need an audit trail for who changed RBAC or model routing.
[01:20] Omar: All control-plane events are logged. There's an audit-log stream we can forward to your SIEM — we provide JSON structured events, and we can also push to syslog or Kinesis depending on your stack.
[01:30] Mark: We're on Splunk and CloudWatch; either works. Can you send a sample payload? Last week's example had some fields renamed (I think KV cache was written as KV cash in the auto transcript) and we want the canonical schema.
[01:42] Omar: Sure, I'll send a schema and samples — you'll get both syslog (text) and JSON event examples. The keys include user_id, actor_email, action, resource, request_id, timestamp, and details (which can be truncated per retention policy).
[01:56] Maya: On retention — Riverbank, what are your regulatory needs for pilot telemetry vs. content? Anita, can you clarify?
[02:02] Anita: For pilot/demo data, legal wants message content retained for 90 days then purged; audit logs need to be kept for seven years for certain financial investigations, but we can set a shorter window for the POC if necessary. However, we need assurance logs won't be deleted prematurely.
[02:18] Omar: Okay. Two layers: application content (user inputs and LLM outputs) and control-plane/audit logs. For the hosted POC we default to 30-day content retention, 365-day audit logs. But we can configure retention policies per workspace: we can extend audit retention to 7 years on Dedicated or Private deployments, and with our add-on long-term archive for hosted.
[02:36] Lisa: That add-on — is it encrypted with customer keys? We have a BYOK requirement for anything beyond 90 days.
[02:42] Omar: Yes — for archive/long-term storage we support BYOK via KMS integrations. We also support HSM-backed keys for on-prem/private installs. For hosted, the archive bucket can be encrypted with your KMS key and access audited.
[02:54] Mark: Good. On the SOC2 artifact — Maya, can you re-share the latest SOC 2 Type II? We need to review controls mapping for logging and incident management.
[03:02] Maya: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC2 and our security whitepaper to the deal in CRM after the call.
[03:08] Lisa: Also curious about console access — admin sessions, api tokens, are tokens rotated automatically?
[03:14] Omar: API keys are long-lived by default but we support short-lived STS tokens and can integrate with your identity provider for session management. We also log token issuance and revocation in the audit stream.
[03:24] Anita: Does Redwood provide evidence for SOC2 during POC — like logs or screenshots for a snapshot audit?
[03:30] Maya: We can provide the SOC2 report and a controls mapping doc. For deeper evidence we'll need an executed NDA or an evidence-sharing agreement — but we can start with redacted screenshots and log samples.
[03:40] Mark: Sounds reasonable. Another item: network access — during the pilot we want an option to run in our VPC or at least have a private link. What are the options?
[03:48] Omar: Three options: hosted with private-link, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud with VPC peering), or Redwood Private — a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. For the pilot, private-link is typically quickest to set up.
[03:59] Lisa: Is private-link data path encrypted end-to-end and does it traverse public internet?
[04:04] Omar: Private-link keeps traffic on the cloud provider backbone; TLS over the wire plus mTLS for service-to-service. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. We'll provide the network diagrams in the security pack.
[04:16] Maya: I'll include diagrams and the private-link setup doc.
[04:19] Mark: Thank you. A small point on the audit events — can we configure obfuscation/redaction for PII in the logs? We can't send raw consumer PII to Splunk without masking.
[04:28] Omar: Yes, we have a configurable redaction pipeline. You can choose fields to mask or hash (we support tokenization). For the pilot we can enable PII redaction at edge.
[04:36] Anita: That helps. For retention of message content — you said 30 days by default — can we reduce it to 14 during pilot to minimize blast radius?
[04:42] Omar: We can. For hosted we can set workspace retention to 14 days; for Dedicated/Private, retention policies are fully customer-configurable. But note: if you need to debug model regressions we sometimes ask for samples — that can be done via opt-in snapshot sharing.
[04:56] Lisa: About encryption keys — will Redwood have access to the keys if we use BYOK?
[05:00] Omar: With BYOK in hosted mode, keys are in your KMS and Redwood gets an encrypted reference; we never have plaintext access. For Private deployments you manage keys entirely.
[05:08] Maya: Quick question for Anita — any regulatory constraints around data residency for the pilot data?
[05:13] Anita: Pilot traffic will contain some EU customer data. We need EU residency for those records and audit logs should stay in the EU region if possible.
[05:20] Omar: Supported — we can pin storage to a region and send logs to a regional SIEM endpoint. We'll document the regionning options. (small laugh) regionning — sorry, regioning.
[05:30] Mark: (laughs) transcription note for later.
[05:33] Maya: Alright, next: incident response integration. Do you ship to PagerDuty or just email?
[05:38] Omar: We integrate with PagerDuty, Slack, and can send SNMP traps. Incident events are forwarded from our monitoring pipeline and also appear in the audit logs with correlation IDs.
[05:47] Lisa: We'll want a runbook for POC incidents and an escalation path.
[05:50] Maya: We'll attach a short runbook and the SLA summary for the pilot.
[05:55] Mark: One technical quirk: last week when we tried a load test, we saw a few timeouts — is that expected on hosted tier?
[06:02] Omar: For low-latency runs the runtime uses batching and KV cache; on hosted the environment is multi-tenant so spikes can cause queuing. For predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated. For the pilot we can bump up concurrency or route test traffic to a reserved pool.
[06:14] Maya: We'll also share the recommended test harness and a short guidance doc for synthetic load runs.
[06:19] Anita: Anything else on compliance side?
[06:22] Lisa: One last item — will Redwood's staff have privileged access to our pilot data for troubleshooting? If yes, how is that audited?
[06:29] Omar: Access is role-based, and privileged sessions are recorded. We have a break-glass process for emergency access that requires approvals and is logged to the audit stream with reason and approver. We can generate a report for any access window.
[06:41] Anita: Good. Please include the break-glass workflow in the docs.
[06:45] Maya: Noted. Omar, will you follow up with the example audit logs and the redaction config?
[06:50] Omar: Yes, I'll post both to the shared drive and link in CRM.
[06:53] Maya: And I'll drop SOC2 and whitepaper. Mark, please send Okta metadata.
[06:58] Mark: Will do.
[07:00] Lisa: Can we schedule the VPC deep dive next week? Prefer mornings 9-11 EST.
[07:05] Maya: I'll propose slots; Omar, are you available next Tuesday morning?
[07:09] Omar: Yes.
[07:11] Maya: Great. Shall we recap?
[07:13] Anita: Sure.
[07:14] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2 & security whitepaper; SE to provide sample audit logs and redaction guide; customer to share Okta metadata and retention constraints; schedule VPC/private deployment deep dive next week. Anything to add?
[07:28] Lisa: No, that covers it.
[07:30] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up in CRM with artifacts.
[07:33] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[07:34] Anita: Thanks.
[07:35] Maya: End call.
